submitted.rationale: Index 2 (Fe0.84Sb0.16) had the highest measured EQE, 0.177%. Hematite is on the hull, and its gap (~2.77 eV) matches the 2.7 eV illumination. Moderate Sb doping appears to help: EQE rose from 0.131% at 12% Sb to 0.177% at 16% Sb. At the 1:1 FeSbO4 composition it fell to 0.005%, even though that phase is stable and has a 2.08 eV gap.

rejected.reason: FeSbO4 composition. It is stable on the hull, but measured EQE was only 0.005%.
Not measured. EQE fell sharply from the Fe-rich end to the 1:1 composition, so the Sb-rich side is unlikely to be better.

consultations.verdict: Support: Fe-rich end is Sb-doped hematite-like; Fe2O3 HSE gap ~2.77 eV, near the 2.7 eV photon energy, while FeSbO4 is stable (Ehull 0.002) with gap 2.08 eV. Both regions absorb; measure Fe-rich end first to anchor, then FeSbO4 region.

Support: FeSbO4 polymorphs sit on or near the hull (0.014 eV/atom), so index 13 (Fe0.51Sb0.49) should form a single-phase rutile FeSbO4 whose gap (~2.1 eV) absorbs 2.7 eV photons. FeSb2O4 (gap 2.38) is also absorbing, but the Sb-rich side is more likely to be Sb-oxide-diluted. Measuring the 1:1 point.

Support: hematite is on the hull and its gap (~2.77 eV) matches the 2.7 eV illumination. The measured EQE is 25× higher at the Fe-rich end (0.131%) than at FeSbO4 (0.005%), so the photoactive phase is Sb-modified hematite. Index 2 (16% Sb) is close to the best point measured so far, where moderate Sb doping could still raise conductivity before FeSbO4 dilutes it.
